classification.difficultyReason: Requires counting overlapping cyclic groups and applying the generalised pigeonhole principle.

content.prompt: Prove that among ten people seated at a round table with fourteen chairs, there are three consecutive chairs that are occupied.

answer.short:
There are 14 cyclic groups of three consecutive chairs. Each occupied chair belongs to three groups, giving $10\times3=30$ occupied-chair memberships.

If each group contained at most two people, there would be at most $14\times2=28$ memberships. Hence some group has all three chairs occupied.
answer.worked:
Label the chairs $1,2,\ldots,14$ around the table. Consider the 14 groups of three consecutive chairs, including the wraparound groups $\{13,14,1\}$ and $\{14,1,2\}$.

Each occupied chair belongs to exactly three groups. Thus the ten people contribute $10\times3=30$ occupied-chair memberships across these 14 groups.

If every group contained at most two people, the total would be at most $14\times2=28$. Since $30>28$, the generalised pigeonhole principle guarantees that some group contains three people. Its three consecutive chairs are therefore all occupied.
